clue.text: Prime Minister lost plot

blocks.note: first meaning: Anthony ..., British Prime Minister 1955-57
second meaning: the garden mankind lost, as in Milton's Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A premier who has lost the plot, mentally adrift in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost plot' reads as the idiom for going mad, but a plot is a patch of ground, and the lost one is the Garden of Paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a twentieth-century British premier's surname and the biblical garden from which Adam and Eve were expelled.

clue.text: Good person overcomes hesitation about making porn

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for hesitation is read the other way
in a down clue, one thing that overcomes another sits over and around it, so it encloses it

blocks.note: a saint, abbreviated St
the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A virtuous person gets over their doubts about producing pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint's two letters wrap round the hesitation written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or indecent material, a common informal synonym for pornography.

clue.text: Speaker's lacking followers familiar with Congress

indicators.note: a speaker's version is the spoken one, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

blocks.note: someone not chased has nobody following them

explanation.surface: A politician talks of being without supporters while knowing their way round the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress with a capital C suggests Washington; here it is sexual congress, intercourse, so someone familiar with it is not chaste.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress is an old word for sexual intercourse, and being unchaste means having had sexual relations, especially outside approved bounds.

clue.text: Hard-working, when our team falls kind of flat

indicators.note: when something falls it drops out of the word, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: diligent in study
the people on our side are us

explanation.surface: A diligent player's spirits sink flat when their side loses.
explanation.walkthrough: The team's letters come off the end of the word for hard-working.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a one-room apartment, so studio names a type of flat.

clue.text: Vaccine nurses finally review my body parts

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the following word, so only its closing letter is kept
to nurse something is to hold it close, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a jab is an injection, informally a vaccination
the last letter of review
my can be replaced by the impersonal possessive one's

explanation.surface: Someone checks over their body after a vaccination.
explanation.walkthrough: My becomes one's, the impersonal form of a possessive, giving the last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The jawbones are the bones of the jaw, the mandible and maxilla, so they are parts of the body.

clue.text: President almost evacuated troops behind jets

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter is dropped
an evacuated word has had its insides emptied out, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: Joe Biden, US President
the first and last letters of troops

explanation.surface: A president nearly pulled soldiers out from behind the fighter planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind jets' looks like a military position, but it is the definition: jets of water aimed at one's behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a bathroom fixture that sprays water to wash the bottom, so the plural are jets for the rear.

clue.text: Pretty as a dog may be

blocks.note: first meaning: attractive, charming
second meaning: retrieving a thrown stick or ball

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pretty puppy, but the second meaning is the dog's action of bringing things back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning attractive and also the present participle of the verb to retrieve something.

clue.text: Deployed spy on his suggestion

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: An agent was sent to watch a man because someone suggested it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnosis works by suggestion, the planting of ideas in a receptive mind, so the two are closely linked.

clue.text: Tom Daley inverts, jumping without restraint

indicators.note: letters that are jumping around move out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: The Olympic diver Tom Daley flips upside down as he leaps freely from the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inverts' sounds like a reversal signal for a diver, but it is just fodder; jumping does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting demonstratively means openly showing feelings, i.e. without holding back or restraining emotion.

clue.text: Celebrated crosses Switzerland scored

indicators.note: to cross something can mean to stretch across it, so one word straddles and encloses the other

blocks.note: famous, well known
CH is Switzerland's international code (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A famous player crosses into Switzerland and gets a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' suggests a goal, but here it means cut with marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notched has had small cuts made in it, which is one sense of scored.

clue.text: Arab newspaper follows Love Island

indicators.note: follows says the first named piece is placed after the others in the line

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of zero
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
the i is a British daily paper

explanation.surface: A tabloid report on the reality TV show Love Island featuring an Arab contestant.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality dating show; here it is split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman, a country on the Arabian Peninsula, so an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: According to Spooner, Starmer put a stop to vessel

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so we do the same

blocks.note: Keir is Starmer's first name; to put a stop to something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer, the UK Prime Minister, shuts down a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of Keir and ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A can holding beer is a container, and vessel is a general word for any receptacle for liquid.

clue.text: Arrangement at 6:30 with facility

blocks.note: first meaning: on a clock face at half past six both pointers face the bottom
second meaning: easily, without effort

explanation.walkthrough: The time reads like an appointment; it is the position of a clock's pointers, both hanging at the bottom of the dial.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning hands down means winning easily, so the idiom means with ease, which is what facility means here.

clue.text: Wife drawn in by computer games gets immersed

indicators.note: something drawn in by another is pulled inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: The Sims is a series of life-simulation computer games
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife hooked on video games becomes completely absorbed in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets immersed' seems to describe the gaming wife; it is the definition, taken literally as being in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who swims is in water, literally immersed in it, as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: Nerds perhaps giving evening courses

indicators.note: this marks a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, is what would give the word before it, perhaps

blocks.note: reverse clue: this word is the result of an instruction to place D, for daughter, inside its other four letters, and the grid word spells that instruction

explanation.surface: Geeks offering night classes at the local college.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as D IN NERS, an instruction to put D (daughter) inside NERS, and the result is NERDS. 'Evening courses' suggests adult education but means meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinners are evening meals, each made up of courses, so a pun on courses as classes and as dishes.

clue.text: Slight men caught in front

indicators.note: caught here means heard, so we want what the word sounds like

blocks.note: to dis (diss) is to slight or disrespect
men are guys

explanation.surface: Small men are caught at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective for the men; it is a verb, to insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguise is a false outward show, and a front is likewise a misleading appearance hiding the truth.

clue.text: Underwear supply Nigel Farage finally packs for one

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, so only the closing letter is kept
read as supple-y, i.e. flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order
to pack something is to stuff it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the letters as written
the last letter of Farage
e.g., for example, means for one

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage ends up packing lingerie for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Supply is read as the adverb from supple, flexibly. The shuffled letters take the abbreviation for 'for one' after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, often sheer dressing gown or nightdress worn by women, so a kind of underwear.

clue.text: Spill the beans about Tory fringe up to no good

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the others

blocks.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
C for Conservative
the hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: An insider reveals that the Conservative extremists are plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory fringe' looks like the right-wing edge of the party; it is two separate pieces placed inside the confession word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scheming means plotting in an underhand way, which is being up to no good.

clue.text: Sullen doggers regularly scrubbed vehicles

indicators.note: letters scrubbed at regular intervals means every other one is wiped out and the rest kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters

explanation.surface: Grumpy people indulging in outdoor sex had their cars cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogging is British slang for sex in parked cars, which makes 'vehicles' sound like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledges are vehicles on runners for travel over snow or ice.

clue.text: Celebrate lately — Brussels account is beginning to expand

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
a log is a record or account
taken as written
the first letter of expand

explanation.surface: A recent celebration that the Brussels budget is starting to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lately' seems to mean recently, but it belongs to the definition: celebrating the late, i.e. the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogise is to praise highly, especially someone who has died, so it is celebrating the late.

clue.text: Filipino native has some time left over

indicators.note: some means just a part, so the answer sits inside the words that follow
over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: found running through the two words

explanation.surface: A man from the Philippines has spare time on his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' suggests a person; it is a plant, the tree native to the Philippines that yields this resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from a Philippine tree, Canarium, so it is native to the islands.

clue.text: Sign of summer beginning in Santorini

blocks.note: first meaning: the mathematical symbol for a sum, used by one who adds up
second meaning: the first letter of the island's name written in Greek

explanation.walkthrough: A summer here is one who sums, not the season; and Santorini in Greek starts with the same letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital Greek letter is the summation symbol in maths and the initial of the Greek name of the island.

clue.text: Key groups like circumventing tax

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go around, so one word encircles the other

blocks.note: as means like
a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: Important groups are said to be avoiding tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key groups' reads as important groups; a key is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Atolls are ring-shaped coral reefs or island chains, and a key (cay) is a small low island.

clue.text: When exposed, Stormy Daniels makes these?

definitions.text: When exposed, Stormy Daniels makes these?

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the outside letters go and the middle stays
a stormy sea churns about, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the middle letters of when
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A scandal-hit adult film star hits the news whenever details come out.
explanation.walkthrough: Stormy Daniels is the adult-film actor at the centre of the Trump hush-money case. Her first name is the anagram signal, and 'exposed' hints at nudity but strips a word; the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught up in a public scandal puts a person's name in the large-type titles at the top of front-page news stories.

clue.text: A female and male prepared to get aroused

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up from its ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A woman and a man get ready for passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame means on fire, and figuratively burning with passion or excitement, i.e. aroused.

clue.text: Always the same outfit

blocks.note: first meaning: unvarying, constant
second meaning: standard clothing worn by members of a group

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone who wears the same clothes every day; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning unchanging and consistent, and a noun for the regulation dress of a school, army or team.

clue.text: Setter retracted error one's there to catch

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: gel is something that makes a liquid set
a slip is a small mistake

explanation.surface: A crossword setter withdraws a mistake that was there to trap solvers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler; it is a setting agent. Leg slip is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side, placed for catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder at leg slip is stationed purely to take catches off the batsman's glances.

clue.text: Make-up artist impressed by Julia Roberts

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so the answer lies stamped inside the following words

blocks.note: running across the actress's two names

explanation.surface: A cosmetics expert is wowed by the film star Julia Roberts.
explanation.walkthrough: A make-up artist sounds like a cosmetics professional; it is someone skilled at making things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar invents falsehoods, i.e. makes things up, so is literally an artist of making up.

clue.text: Quince takes job, turning up for stressful work?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means flipping so the bottom comes to the top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself, so their name means me
an op is an operation, a job

explanation.surface: The setter Quince takes on an assignment that turns out to be stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress here is metrical: a poem is built on patterns of stressed syllables, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is organised by stressed and unstressed syllables, so a poem is a piece of writing full of stresses.

clue.text: Letters delivered in the wrong place

definitions.text: Letters delivered in the wrong place

blocks.clueFragment: Letters delivered in the wrong place
blocks.note: surface reading: post sent to the wrong address
setter's reading: letters of the alphabet put in the wrong position within a word

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a postal blunder; the letters are alphabetic ones, placed wrongly when a word is written.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting characters in the wrong order or position within a word is an orthographic error.
